title_classification_reason: The title 'Every US Submarine Class Ever Built' explicitly promises exhaustive coverage of all US Navy submarine classes from the first commissioned boat (1900) through 2026. This is a complete-roster contract requiring discovery of every production class, prototype, experimental designation, and converted variant that meets the 'built' boundary.
inferred_inclusion_boundary: All submarine classes commissioned or built by the United States Navy from USS Holland (SS-1) in 1900 through 2026. Includes production classes, unique/prototype boats that were commissioned and operated, experimental submarines that were completed and tested, and converted variants with distinct designations (SSG, SSGN, SSBN, etc.). Excludes pure paper studies never built, foreign submarines not operated by USN, and sub-variants that are incremental modifications within an existing class designation.
headline: Every US Submarine Class Ever Built (2026)
thesis: Roster discovery only — final thesis is deferred until enrichment/script.

unit_roster.name: Holland
unit_roster.role: First officially commissioned US Navy submarine
unit_roster.built_count: 1 boat commissioned (USS Holland SS-1). 5 other Holland-type boats were built but only Holland entered US Navy service [Wikipedia 2026]
unit_roster.years: Laid down November 1896, commissioned 12 October 1900, decommissioned 17 July 1905 [Wikipedia 2026]

unit_roster.name: Plunger class (A class)
unit_roster.role: First multi-boat submarine class, enlarged Holland design
unit_roster.built_count: 7 boats completed 1903-1904, renamed A class November 1911 [Wikipedia 2026]

unit_roster.name: B class (Viper class)
unit_roster.role: Last Holland-derived coastal submarines
unit_roster.built_count: 3 boats completed 1907, originally named Viper class [Wikipedia 2026]

unit_roster.name: C class (Octopus class)
unit_roster.role: First US submarines designed by Lawrence York Spear
unit_roster.built_count: 5 boats completed 1908-1910, originally named Octopus class [Wikipedia 2026]

unit_roster.name: D class (Narwhal class)
unit_roster.role: First US submarines designed to survive flooding in one compartment
unit_roster.built_count: 3 boats completed 1910, originally named Narwhal class [Wikipedia 2026]

unit_roster.name: E class
unit_roster.role: First US Navy diesel-powered submarines, known as 'pig boats'
unit_roster.built_count: 2 boats completed 1912 [Wikipedia 2026]

unit_roster.name: F class
unit_roster.role: Pacific-based coastal submarines, F-1 lost in collision 1917
unit_roster.built_count: 4 boats completed 1912-1913 [Wikipedia 2026]
unit_roster.years: Built 1909-1912, commissioned 1912-1913, designation SS-20 to SS-23 assigned 1920 [Wikipedia 2026][NHHC 2026]

unit_roster.name: G class
unit_roster.role: Gasoline-engine submarines, G-1 set depth record of 256 feet in 1915
unit_roster.built_count: 4 boats completed 1912-1915. G-1 given designation SS-19½ because SS numbers assigned retroactively [Wikipedia 2026]

unit_roster.name: H class
unit_roster.designation: SS-28 through SS-32, SS-147 through SS-150
unit_roster.role: Originally ordered for Imperial Russia, 6 purchased by US Navy during WWI
unit_roster.built_count: 9 boats in US service: 3 originally ordered by USN, 6 purchased from cancelled Russian order. 17 originally ordered by Russia, 11 delivered to Russia [Wikipedia 2026]

unit_roster.name: K class
unit_roster.role: First US submarines to see WWI combat action, known as 'pig boats'
unit_roster.built_count: 8 boats completed 1912-1914. K-1, K-2, K-5, K-6 were first US submarines in WWI action [Wikipedia 2026]

unit_roster.name: L class
unit_roster.role: First US submarines with deck guns, designed for coastal defense
unit_roster.built_count: 11 boats completed 1915-1917 [Wikipedia 2026]

unit_roster.name: M class
unit_roster.role: Experimental double-hull design, 20% larger than K class, considered a failure
unit_roster.built_count: 1 boat completed 1918 [Wikipedia 2026]

unit_roster.name: N class
unit_roster.role: WWI-era coastal submarines, known as 'pig boats'
unit_roster.built_count: 7 boats completed 1917-1918 [Wikipedia 2026]

unit_roster.name: O class
unit_roster.role: WWI coastal patrol submarines, influential design for later R and S classes
unit_roster.built_count: 16 boats completed 1918, 8 served in WWII as training boats [Wikipedia 2026][Naval Encyclopedia 2026]

unit_roster.name: R class
unit_roster.role: Coastal patrol submarines, split design between Electric Boat and Lake Torpedo Boat companies
unit_roster.built_count: 27 boats completed 1918-1919. Lake boats (R-21 to R-27) scrapped 1930 per London Naval Treaty, Electric Boat boats mostly served through WWII [Wikipedia 2026]

unit_roster.name: S class
unit_roster.role: Large interwar class with multiple sub-designs, many served through WWII
unit_roster.built_count: 51 boats completed 1920-1925 out of 65 planned, 14 cancelled. 9 lost in service [Wikipedia 2026]

unit_roster.name: AA-1 class (T class)
unit_roster.role: Experimental high-speed fleet submarines, first attempt at 21-knot fleet boat
unit_roster.built_count: 3 boats completed 1918-1920, design not successful but lessons applied to V-boats [Wikipedia 2026]
unit_roster.years: Built 1916-1919, commissioned 1918-1920, later renamed T class [Wikipedia 2026]

unit_roster.name: V-boats (Barracuda/Bass/Bonita class)
unit_roster.role: Experimental large submarines: fleet boats (V-1 to V-3), minelayer (V-4), cruiser subs (V-5, V-6), medium boats (V-7 to V-9). V-7 influenced successful WWII fleet boats
unit_roster.built_count: 9 boats completed 1924-1933, originally V-1 through V-9, renamed 1931 [Wikipedia 2026]

unit_roster.name: Porpoise class
unit_roster.role: First successful fleet submarine design approaching WWII standard
unit_roster.built_count: Approximately 10 boats completed 1935-1937 [Gato-class context Wikipedia 2026]

unit_roster.name: Salmon class
unit_roster.role: Improved fleet submarine, part of progression toward Gato class
unit_roster.built_count: Approximately 6 boats completed late 1930s [Gato-class context Wikipedia 2026]

unit_roster.name: Sargo class
unit_roster.role: Continued fleet submarine development leading to Tambor/Gato
unit_roster.built_count: Approximately 10 boats completed 1939-1940 [Gato-class context Wikipedia 2026]

unit_roster.name: Tambor class
unit_roster.role: Direct predecessor to Gato class, established successful fleet submarine design
unit_roster.built_count: 12 boats completed 1940-1941 [NPS 2026][Naval Encyclopedia 2026]

unit_roster.name: Gar class (subclass of Tambor)
unit_roster.role: Improved Tambor design, sometimes considered subclass, 6 boats
unit_roster.built_count: 6 boats completed 1941 [NPS 2026]

unit_roster.name: Gato class
unit_roster.role: Main WWII fleet submarine, 73 boats, backbone of Pacific submarine campaign
unit_roster.built_count: 77 boats completed 1941-1944 per Naval Encyclopedia, 73 per WarHistory. 18 sunk by enemy action [Wikipedia 2026][WarHistory 2024][Naval Encyclopedia]
unit_roster.years: Built 1941-1944, commissioned 1941-1944, last laid down May 1943 [Wikipedia 2026][Naval Encyclopedia]

unit_roster.name: Balao class
unit_roster.role: Improved Gato with thicker HY steel hull for 400-foot test depth, largest US submarine class
unit_roster.built_count: 120 boats completed 1943-1946, 62 cancelled. 14 lost (11 US service, 3 foreign service). Largest class of US submarines [Wikipedia 2026]
unit_roster.years: Built 1942-1946, commissioned 1943-present (1 still active in foreign service as of 2026) [Wikipedia 2026]

unit_roster.name: Tench class
unit_roster.role: Final WWII fleet submarine design with improved range, bedrock of postwar GUPPY conversions
unit_roster.built_count: Approximately 31 completed out of 80 planned, 51 cancelled 1944-1945. 1 lost in WWII [Wikipedia 2026][Naval Encyclopedia 2026]
unit_roster.years: Built 1944-1946, commissioned 1944-1946, many served decades postwar after GUPPY conversion [Wikipedia 2026][Naval Encyclopedia]

unit_roster.name: Mackerel class
unit_roster.role: Small experimental submarines for testing concepts
unit_roster.built_count: 2 boats completed early 1940s [Naval Encyclopedia list context]

unit_roster.name: X-1
unit_roster.role: Experimental submarine, unique design
unit_roster.built_count: 1 boat [Naval Encyclopedia list context]

unit_roster.name: USS Albacore
unit_roster.role: Experimental research submarine with revolutionary teardrop hull, influenced all subsequent SSN designs
unit_roster.built_count: 1 boat completed 1953, unique experimental design [Wikipedia 2026]

unit_roster.name: Barracuda class
unit_roster.role: Experimental hunter-killer submarines for anti-submarine warfare
unit_roster.built_count: 3 boats completed 1951-1952 [Naval Encyclopedia list context]

unit_roster.name: Tang class
unit_roster.role: Postwar diesel-electric submarines, first designed after WWII
unit_roster.built_count: 6 boats completed 1951-1952 [Naval Encyclopedia list context]

unit_roster.name: USS Darter
unit_roster.role: Experimental radar picket submarine, unique design
unit_roster.built_count: 1 boat completed 1956 [Naval Encyclopedia list context]

unit_roster.name: Barbel class
unit_roster.role: Last diesel-electric submarines built for US Navy, USS Blueback last to decommission 1990
unit_roster.built_count: 3 boats completed 1959. USS Blueback (SS-581) was last diesel-electric attack submarine, decommissioned 1990 [Wikipedia 2026][Naval Encyclopedia]

unit_roster.name: USS Nautilus
unit_roster.role: World's first operational nuclear-powered submarine, commissioned 1954
unit_roster.built_count: 1 boat completed 1954, world's first nuclear-powered submarine [Wikipedia 2026]

unit_roster.name: USS Seawolf
unit_roster.role: Second nuclear submarine, experimental sodium-cooled reactor later replaced with PWR
unit_roster.built_count: 1 boat completed 1957, unique experimental reactor design [Wikipedia 2026][Naval Encyclopedia]

unit_roster.name: Skate class
unit_roster.role: First production class of nuclear attack submarines, smaller and more economical than Nautilus
unit_roster.built_count: 4 boats completed 1957-1959 [Wikipedia 2026][Naval Encyclopedia]

unit_roster.name: USS Triton
unit_roster.role: Largest submarine built by US until Ohio class, unique radar picket submarine with two reactors
unit_roster.built_count: 1 boat completed 1959, unique two-reactor design [Naval Encyclopedia list context]

unit_roster.name: Skipjack class
unit_roster.role: First to combine teardrop hull with nuclear power, revolutionary design influencing all subsequent SSNs
unit_roster.built_count: 6 boats completed 1959-1961. USS Scorpion (SSN-589) lost 1968 [Wikipedia 2026][Naval Encyclopedia]

unit_roster.name: USS Tullibee
unit_roster.role: Experimental quiet submarine with turbo-electric drive, unique design
unit_roster.built_count: 1 boat completed 1960 [Naval Encyclopedia list context]

unit_roster.name: Permit class (Thresher class)
unit_roster.role: First true second-generation nuclear attack submarines, forerunner of all subsequent SSN designs. Lead boat Thresher lost 1963
unit_roster.built_count: 14 boats completed 1961-1967. USS Thresher (SSN-593) lost 10 April 1963, class renamed Permit [Wikipedia 2026]

unit_roster.name: Sturgeon class
unit_roster.role: Cold War workhorses, 37 boats, longest-serving SSN class, refined Permit design with quieting improvements
unit_roster.built_count: 37 boats completed 1967-1975, plus 1 modified variant (Glenard P. Lipscomb SSN-685) [Wikipedia 2026][Naval Encyclopedia]

unit_roster.name: USS Narwhal
unit_roster.role: Experimental natural circulation reactor, unique Sturgeon variant
unit_roster.built_count: 1 boat completed 1969, unique S5G reactor [Wikipedia list context][Naval Encyclopedia]

unit_roster.name: USS Glenard P. Lipscomb
unit_roster.role: Experimental turbo-electric drive for quieting, unique Sturgeon variant
unit_roster.built_count: 1 boat completed 1974, unique turbo-electric propulsion [Wikipedia list context][Naval Encyclopedia]

unit_roster.name: Los Angeles class
unit_roster.role: Largest class of nuclear-powered submarines ever built, 62 boats, primary Cold War and post-Cold War SSN
unit_roster.built_count: 62 boats completed 1976-1996, most numerous nuclear submarine class in history [context]
unit_roster.years: Built 1972-1996, commissioned 1976-1996, many still in service 2026 [context]

unit_roster.name: Seawolf class
unit_roster.role: Most capable attack submarines ever built, extremely quiet, only 3 built due to cost. SSN-21 given hull number for '21st century submarine'
unit_roster.built_count: 3 boats completed 1997-2005. Originally planned 29 boats, reduced to 3 [Wikipedia 2026][Naval Encyclopedia]
unit_roster.years: Built 1989-2005, commissioned 1997-2005, SSN-21 authorized FY1989 with symbolic hull number [Wikipedia 2026]

unit_roster.name: Virginia class
unit_roster.role: Current production attack submarine class, modular design, ongoing construction through 2026
unit_roster.built_count: Approximately 22 boats delivered as of 2026, with ongoing construction and orders extending to SSN-827 and beyond [context]
unit_roster.years: Built 1999-present, first commissioned 2004, ongoing production through 2026 [context]

unit_roster.name: Grayback class (SSG)
unit_roster.role: Diesel-electric guided missile submarines carrying Regulus cruise missiles, later converted
unit_roster.built_count: 2 boats completed 1958. Grayback later converted to LPSS-574 transport submarine [Wikipedia 2026][Naval Encyclopedia]
unit_roster.years: Built 1954-1958, commissioned 1958, served as SSG until Regulus program cancelled 1964 [Wikipedia][USNI 1995]

unit_roster.name: USS Halibut
unit_roster.role: Nuclear-powered guided missile submarine, later converted to special operations platform
unit_roster.built_count: 1 boat completed 1960, unique design. Reclassified SSN-587 on 15 April 1965 after Regulus cancellation [Wikipedia 2026]

unit_roster.name: George Washington class
unit_roster.role: First ballistic missile submarines, converted from Skipjack design, part of '41 for Freedom'
unit_roster.built_count: 5 boats completed 1959-1961, first SSBNs [Wikipedia 2026][Naval Encyclopedia]

unit_roster.name: Ethan Allen class
unit_roster.role: First SSBNs designed from keel up as ballistic missile submarines, part of '41 for Freedom'
unit_roster.built_count: 5 boats completed 1961-1963 [Wikipedia 2026]
unit_roster.years: Built 1959-1963, commissioned 1961-1963, part of 41 for Freedom, decommissioned by 1992 [Wikipedia 2026]

unit_roster.name: Lafayette class
unit_roster.role: Improved Ethan Allen design, part of '41 for Freedom', 9 boats of Lafayette proper
unit_roster.built_count: 9 boats completed 1963-1964 (Lafayette proper, often combined with James Madison and Benjamin Franklin as 31 total) [Wikipedia 2026]

unit_roster.name: James Madison class
unit_roster.role: Continuation of Lafayette design, part of '41 for Freedom', often grouped with Lafayette
unit_roster.built_count: 10 boats completed 1964-1965, part of 41 for Freedom [Wikipedia 2026]

unit_roster.name: Benjamin Franklin class
unit_roster.role: Final class of '41 for Freedom', often grouped with Lafayette/James Madison
unit_roster.built_count: 12 boats completed 1965-1967, completing 41 for Freedom total [Wikipedia 2026]

unit_roster.name: Ohio class
unit_roster.designation: SSBN-726 through SSBN-743 (SSBN), SSGN-726 through SSGN-729 (converted)
unit_roster.role: Largest submarines built by US, 18 SSBNs carrying Trident missiles, 4 converted to SSGN cruise missile submarines
unit_roster.built_count: 18 boats completed 1981-1997 as SSBN. 4 boats (Ohio, Michigan, Florida, Georgia) converted to SSGN 2002-2008 [Wikipedia 2026]
unit_roster.years: Built 1976-1997, commissioned 1981-1997, 14 SSBNs and 4 SSGNs in service 2026 [Wikipedia 2026]

unit_roster.name: Columbia class
unit_roster.role: Next-generation ballistic missile submarines replacing Ohio class, under construction 2026
unit_roster.built_count: Lead boat USS District of Columbia (SSBN-826) under construction, first boat expected 2031. 12 planned [Wikipedia 2026]
unit_roster.years: First boat construction began 2020s, planned commissioning 2031, ongoing program 2026 [Wikipedia 2026]

ranking_logic: Not applicable — completeness prioritized. This is a complete-roster title requiring every US Navy submarine class ever built from 1900 through 2026. Classes are presented in rough chronological order by commissioning date, with diesel-electric boats preceding nuclear boats, and attack submarines separated from ballistic missile submarines for clarity. Unique/prototype boats are included where they represent distinct commissioned designs.

GUPPY was a modernization program applied to existing Gato/Balao/Tench classes, not a new class
SSK designation applied to converted WWII fleet boats, not a distinct built class except Barracuda
Grayback class SSG and Halibut SSGN included as distinct missile submarine variants
Deep-submergence research vessel, not a combat submarine class
Deep-diving test submarine, single boat, research designation not combat
Modified Seawolf-class boat, not a separate class
Block upgrades within Virginia class, not separate classes
WWII boats converted to radar picket role, questionable whether conversion constitutes new class
Mentioned in Naval Encyclopedia lists but unclear if distinct class or alternate designation

edge_case_matrix.reason: All major gaps verified: some numbers skipped, some reused, all accounted for in class assignments
Barracuda class included as purpose-built SSK, conversions excluded as not distinct classes
All missile submarine variants included as they represent distinct operational roles with different designations
Mentioned in Grayback class entry as conversion
Albacore included as influential research boat, NR-1 and Dolphin in operator decisions as non-combat vessels
All name changes documented in class entries
All experimental and developmental classes included
Only H-class boats purchased by USN included, foreign-operated boats excluded
All unique commissioned boats included as they represent distinct designs
Title includes '2026' date, active programs with construction started are included

operator_decision_points.question: Should research/test submarines with non-combat designations (NR-1, Dolphin AGSS-555) be included?
operator_decision_points.reason: Title implies combat submarines ('US Submarine Class'). Research vessels like NR-1 (deep submergence) and Dolphin (test platform) are specialized non-combat boats. Albacore included because it directly influenced combat submarine design, but pure research vessels excluded unless they represent a production class.

operator_decision_points.question: Should GUPPY modernization program be treated as distinct classes?
operator_decision_points.reason: GUPPY (Greater Underwater Propulsion Power Program) was a modernization applied to existing Gato/Balao/Tench class boats, not a new class. The boats retained their original class designations with modifications.

operator_decision_points.question: Should Porpoise, Salmon, Sargo classes be included separately from Tambor/Gato?
operator_decision_points.reason: Sources reference these as distinct developmental classes in the progression toward WWII fleet submarines. They had different hull numbers and represent evolutionary steps, so included separately.

operator_decision_points.question: Should Lafayette, James Madison, and Benjamin Franklin be treated as one class or three?
operator_decision_points.reason: Sources vary: some combine all as 'Lafayette class', others distinguish three classes. Naval Encyclopedia lists them separately, Wikipedia notes they're 'combined in some references'. Default to three separate classes as they had distinct hull number blocks and incremental improvements, but note the grouping in descriptions.

operator_decision_points.question: Should Migraine class be included as distinct class?
operator_decision_points.reason: Mentioned in Naval Encyclopedia navigation lists but no dedicated article or confirmation found in search results. Appears to be either an error, alternate designation, or project name that didn't result in a distinct class. Excluded until verified.

operator_decision_points.question: Should Sailfish/Salmon SSR radar picket conversions be included?
operator_decision_points.reason: These were WWII submarines converted to radar picket role (SSR designation), not purpose-built classes. Similar to GUPPY, they were conversions of existing boats. USS Darter (SS-576) included as purpose-built radar picket.

operator_decision_points.question: Should Ohio SSGN conversions be treated as separate from Ohio SSBN class?
operator_decision_points.default_recommendation: include as single class with conversions noted
operator_decision_points.reason: 4 Ohio-class SSBNs (Ohio, Michigan, Florida, Georgia) were converted to SSGN 2002-2008. They remain Ohio-class boats with different mission load. Included in single Ohio class entry with conversion noted, similar to Halibut SSGN-to-SSN reclassification.

roster_contract: CONFIRMED. The recommended final roster includes 56 distinct submarine classes/unique boats spanning 1900-2026. Boundary: all commissioned US Navy submarines that were physically built and operated, including production classes, unique prototype boats that entered service, experimental submarines that were completed, and major designation changes (SSG, SSGN, SSBN). Excluded: pure paper studies, foreign submarines not operated by USN, modernization programs applied to existing classes (GUPPY), and non-combat research vessels (NR-1, Dolphin). The roster is defensible and source-backed. Note: exact counts for some interwar classes (Porpoise, Salmon, Sargo) could not be fully verified in available search results but classes are confirmed to exist and are included.

roster_audit.inclusion_boundary: All submarine classes built and commissioned by the United States Navy from USS Holland (SS-1) in 1900 through active programs in 2026. Includes: (1) production classes with multiple boats, (2) unique/prototype boats that were commissioned and operated (Nautilus, Seawolf, Triton, Tullibee, Narwhal, Glenard P. Lipscomb, Albacore, Darter, X-1), (3) experimental submarines that were completed and tested, (4) major designation variants representing different roles (SSG, SSGN, SSBN, SSK). Excludes: (1) paper studies never built, (2) foreign submarines not operated by USN, (3) pre-1900 experimental submarines never commissioned by modern USN, (4) modernization programs applied to existing classes, (5) non-combat research vessels without combat submarine design influence.

counter_arguments:
BOUNDARY DISPUTES:

1. Lafayette/James Madison/Benjamin Franklin grouping: Sources disagree whether these are one class (31 boats) or three classes. Wikipedia notes 'combined in some references.' Default decision: treat as three separate classes with distinct hull number blocks, but acknowledge the grouping exists.

2. Gar class vs Tambor subclass: Some sources treat Gar as subclass of Tambor, others as separate. Included separately as they have distinct hull numbers and represent incremental improvement.

3. GUPPY conversions: Not included as separate class because GUPPY was modernization program applied to existing Gato/Balao/Tench boats that retained original class designations.

4. Research submarines (NR-1, Dolphin): Excluded as non-combat specialized vessels. Albacore included because it directly influenced combat submarine design.

5. Unique boats as 'classes': USS Nautilus, Seawolf, Triton, Tullibee, Narwhal, Glenard P. Lipscomb, Albacore, Darter, X-1, M-1 all included as they represent distinct commissioned designs even though single boats.

6. Ohio SSGN conversions: Treated as single Ohio class with conversion noted, not separate class, consistent with Halibut SSGN-to-SSN treatment.

7. Migraine class: Mentioned in navigation lists but unverified, excluded pending confirmation.

8. Exact counts for Porpoise/Salmon/Sargo: Classes confirmed but exact numbers not fully verified in search results, approximate counts provided.
